S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

patient_info.stressor_event: Death of a close family member
patient_info.stressor: After Nguyen’s father died unexpectedly, he took on the practical role of organizing family records, memorial photographs, and donation receipts for the Vietnamese community events his father had supported. Over the next 9 months, his grief-focused effort to make sense of small inconsistencies in paperwork and online messages hardened into a fixed belief that certain people had deliberately concealed the truth around the death, despite repeated reassurance and clear contradictory documentation. He continued working as a systems analyst and maintained much of his routine, but the belief increasingly shaped family conversations and made relatives wary of discussing the loss with him. Nguyen eventually contacted a psychiatrist through his workplace health plan, partly because he wanted an outside professional to review whether his conclusions were reasonable.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and donation emails all line up, but when I compare the timestamps, missing attachments, and the way certain community members avoid my questions, it’s obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father’s death.

additional_requirement_1.name: Additional Requirement 1
additional_requirement_1.description: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications
additional_requirement_1.manifestation: I still go to work, handle my projects, pay my bills, and keep my normal routine; the main place things get tense is when I bring up my questions about my father’s records with family or community members.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: My job performance has mostly stayed steady, but some relatives have started avoiding conversations with me because they know I may bring up the records and what I think was concealed.

duration.name: Duration
duration.manifestation: This has been going on for about nine months, since the period after my father died and I started sorting through his records and messages.
